inspected_anchors: Paper pp1–4: processing/structure/reporting agents, MCP/Sachs demonstration and future quantitative/counterfactual work
claims: CausalAgent describes processing, structure-learning and reporting agents, LangGraph routing, GLM-4.6 and MCP tool scheduling.
The four-page paper demonstrates a Sachs dataset conversational workflow and links its public code.
Its future-work section includes quantitative effect estimation, counterfactual modules and expert feedback in high-risk domains.

inspected_anchors: Paper pp1–5: human principal, notebooks, overlap, ACIC/LaLonde evaluation
claims: oci-agent places an accountable human principal over actor/critic personas and reproducible notebooks using deterministic causal libraries.
It targets point-in-time effects under supplied unconfoundedness, with cross-fitted AIPW and design diagnostics.
Authors report 231 ACIC datasets, a ten-dataset scaffolding comparison, and disguised LaLonde evaluations; the critic declines most PSID replications for poor overlap.
sources.limits: Static paper evidence; no live model call, bank data or independent acceptance.

inspected_anchors: Paper pp1–3,6,10,29: scenes, private ground truth, abstention and100/953 exam
claims: CausalDS provides narrated synthetic SCM scenes, data files, a separate observation model and private scoring artifacts.
Interventional and counterfactual targets have separate identification decisions, with abstention on nonidentifiable tasks.
The paper reports a 100-scene exam sampled from 953 scenes and finds that symbolic success, interval quality, abstention and cost can diverge.

The authors report domain-dependent calibration, false-positive/false-negative patterns and retrieval failures.
The requirements discussion explicitly notes developer-defined requirements; paper counts differ across sections and should not be treated as a stable release inventory.

inspected_anchors: Paper pp3,6,9: data inspection, method selection, CPDAG/PAG ambiguity and benchmark call
claims: The paper describes causal-learn+ with agent assistance for data inspection, assumption elicitation, method selection and interpretation around formal discovery algorithms.
It distinguishes agent suggestions, user decisions, algorithm parameters and graph outputs, and explains why CPDAG/PAG ambiguity must remain visible.
It calls for future benchmarks of data diagnosis, method selection and calibrated interpretation.
